note: Rules are paraphrased from the thread; each cites the tweet it comes from. Fetch the thread with the `fetch` method for the original text.

rules.rule: The jacket hem must sit level when seen from the side, or hang slightly lower at the front than at the back.
rules.why: Patterns graded up for a larger body often lack cloth at the front, so the belly lifts the front hem above the back hem.
rules.check: Stand side-on to a mirror. If the front of the hem rides higher than the back, ask a tailor (or an MTM maker) for more front length.

rules.why: A high rise lengthens the leg line. A low rise sits under the stomach and is unflattering on a heavier figure.
rules.check: The waistband should sit at or above the navel and not slide below the belly.

rules.rule: Do not wear super slim-fit trousers; the jacket or top should flow into the legs.
rules.why: Narrow legs under a large torso make a disjointed 'popsicle stick' silhouette.
rules.check: From the front, the trouser leg should continue the line of the jacket's side, not taper sharply away from it.

rules.rule: Tailoring must fit without puckering or pulling, with clean drape across the chest.
rules.why: Pulling at the button or chest makes the jacket look too small and shows the body's widest point.
rules.check: Buttoned, there should be no X-shaped creases from the button and no gaps at the lapels.

rules.rule: The coat should end about halfway between the collar and the floor.
rules.why: Classic proportion. A short jacket cuts a large figure at its widest point.
rules.check: Measure collar-to-floor; the hem should sit near the midpoint.

rules.why: A jacket worn open because it cannot close reads as the wrong size.
rules.check: Button it and sit down; it should not strain.

rules.rule: The lapel should end about halfway between the collar and the shoulder seam.
rules.why: Narrow lapels look undersized on a broad chest; balanced lapels keep the proportions in scale.
rules.check: Compare lapel width with the distance from collar to shoulder seam.

rules.rule: Build casual clothes around workwear (chore coats, work jackets, denim, sturdy shirting).
rules.why: A larger or athletic build works with workwear; it often looks better on these builds than on very slim men. Better than squeezing into slim designer cuts.
rules.check: Prefer sturdy fabrics and roomy, boxy cuts over slim fashion cuts.

rules.rule: With jeans, wear a sport coat in a textured cloth (tweed, hopsack), never a smooth suit jacket.
rules.why: Textured sport coats match denim. A smooth suit jacket looks like an orphaned suit.
rules.check: If the jacket has matching trousers, do not wear it with jeans.

rules.rule: Clothes must allow movement: you can hug someone, reach up, and bend down.
rules.why: A garment that is too small looks worse than one that fits, and restricts you.
rules.check: Hug test (top), reach-up test (top length), squat test (trouser rise).

rules.rule: Do not retreat into anonymous clothes; have a point of view (e.g. a fun suit, workwear with good outerwear).
rules.why: 'I can't wear that' often means 'I don't want to be perceived'. A larger build does not limit you to flat-front chinos and a dress shirt.
rules.check: Can you name what the outfit says about you? If not, it is anonymous.

rules.rule: Double-breasted suits and long coats are not off-limits for a larger figure.
rules.why: The common claim 'you can't wear that if you're big' comes from insecurity, not proportion.
rules.check: Judge a style by fit and proportion on your body, not by its category.

rules.rule: Keep combinations coherent rather than wacky; dress for your lifestyle.
rules.why: Clothes that suit what you actually do look natural.
rules.check: Each piece should belong to the same register (workwear with workwear, tailoring with tailoring, textured tailoring as the bridge).

rules.rule: Past roughly size 44, prefer makers who cut separate patterns for larger sizes, or use MTM and a good tailor.
rules.why: Most brands grade every size from one size-40 sample, which throws off proportions at larger sizes; that, plus the slim-fit trend, causes bad shopping experiences.
rules.check: Ask whether a brand's large sizes use their own block; budget for alterations.

rules.rule: Find what fits, decide what you want to communicate, and find a good tailor.
rules.why: Fit is the base; a tailor closes the gap that grading leaves.
rules.check: Have one trusted alteration tailor before you buy tailoring.
